Day 1 in Darwin (Aug 13): Hasan Mahmud took 6-55 as Australia were bowled out for 198. Bangladesh closed on 96-1 with Mominul 35* and Tanzid Hasan 32* (Shadman out for 20) after the pitch flattened in the afternoon. Litton was cleared to play (Aug 12) and bats at 5 or 6. The Aug 14 resolution date points to a Day-2 hundred, which favours the two set batters over Shanto, Mushfiqur and Litton, who are still to bat.

Aug 13 previews: Nashville have 40 pts (12W-2L-4D, GD +21, unbeaten at home) and Miami 38 (11W-2L-5D) before Saturday's Aug 15 game at Geodis Park. FanDuel has Nashville +110, draw +300, Miami +190 (about 44/23/32 no-vig). A Nashville win clinches. Miami need a win or draw plus favourable Aug 19 results (Miami at Philadelphia, Nashville at NYRB), which scenario math puts at about 27% for Miami.

The archive shows no deadly Indonesian quake through Aug 13. The Jun 16 Sigi M6.7 in Central Sulawesi (3 deaths per BNPB) is still the deadliest, with only about 4 days left in the window (to Aug 17). The residual covers a new quake with 4 or more deaths in the final days, a real risk given the low bar and that the question may have been triggered by fresh news.

Pan Pacs night 1 (Aug 12): Walsh won the 50 fly in 24.65, 0.41s ahead of Douglass, and swam on the US mixed medley relay that set a world record. She holds the 50 free world record (23.55, June) and won US Nationals by 0.45s in the same Irvine pool. Douglass has said she will not swim all three of her Aug 15 events.

Night 1 (Aug 12): Ledecky won the 1500 in 15:36.09, 2.53s ahead of Pallister (15:38.62 PB), the closest anyone has come to her at a major meet since 2013. Two hours earlier Pallister won the 200 free over McIntosh. Ledecky's 800 season best (8:08.57) beats Pallister's 8:11.12 and she is unbeaten in major-meet 800s, so she is favoured, but Pallister is in career form. McIntosh is unlikely to swim the 800.

Aug 12-13 betting is nearly level. To lift the trophy, Arsenal are 5/6 and City 19/20 (football365); draw-no-bet is Arsenal -115 and City -105, about 51/49 no-vig. Arsenal are without Saliba and Timber and conceded 3 twice in pre-season. Maresca's City won 2 and drew 1 in pre-season and added Anderson. The match is Aug 16 at the Principality Stadium and goes straight to penalties if level.

After round 1 (Aug 13): Spieth, Thorbjornsen, Knapp, M. Kim and Kitayama lead at -5. Fleetwood, Matsuyama, Scott, Im, Gotterup, Woodland and Cauley are at -4, Schauffele -3, Scheffler -2 (T17), Young -1 and Fitzpatrick E. McIlroy did play but shot 74. With 54 holes left the field is wide open, and Scheffler, 3 back, is still the single most likely winner.

The consensus has narrowed. The Reuters poll (Aug 7) sees +0.5% q/q with net exports +0.3pp, implying domestic demand about +0.2pp. MaceNews consensus (Aug 13) sees +0.6% with domestic +0.3pp and net exports +0.3pp, a tie. The ESP survey (Aug 12) averages 1.67% annualised (about 0.4% q/q), with most expecting imports to fall more than exports. Net exports remain a modest favourite for the Aug 17 release. Private consumption is a small hedge in case the resolver reads the components as C/I/G/NX.

Mercato360 via SenePlus (Aug 6-8): FSF president Abdoulaye Fall made Vieira the absolute priority, and Vieira agreed to negotiate a 4-year 'Horizon 2030' deal. The principle seems agreed, but staff and salary are unresolved and Thiaw's settlement with the Sports Ministry is pending. No official announcement was found through Aug 13. As a fragile, not-yet-official agreement, it is capped at about 0.5.

On Jul 31 the CJP set aside the registrar's objections to Imran's appeal and clubbed it with Uzma Khan's petition; both ask for transfer to Shifa International (Dawn, Aug 1). The News (Aug 13) reports that a bench of Justices Shahid Waheed, Naeem Afghan and Ishtiaq Ibrahim will hear the health and meeting pleas on Aug 18. Shifa, the relief sought, is a slight favourite over PIMS, where all his eye injections have been given.

Fenerbahce announced Romelu Lukaku from Napoli on Aug 12 (Reuters), filling the striker slot they had targeted Watkins for, so they drop sharply. Man Utd's reported interest depended on Zirkzee leaving, but Zirkzee scored for United on Aug 12; Carrick (Aug 14) wants more signings. Watkins was rested from Villa's Aug 12 Super Cup after the World Cup, teen striker Madjo scored, and no new bids were found.

St Pete Polls (Aug 3-4) has Mills 27-29.5 and Elijah 14 with 41-45% undecided. Victory Insights (Aug 4-6) has Mills 28.3 and Elijah 22 with 41.5% undecided; undecideds view Mills 35% negative to 14% positive, and the pollster rates the race 'Lean Elijah'. Reps Luna and Haridopolos endorsed Elijah (Aug 5), who outraised Mills about 3-1 in July ($186K vs $68K cash on hand). On Aug 13 Elijah noted that Trump left Mills off his endorsement reposts. The Aug 18 plurality primary is a toss-up.

No new call by a major figure for wartime elections was found through Aug 13. Fedorov told the NYT he won't go into opposition or be 'dragged' into politics during the war (Euromaidan Press, Aug 10), so he is cut. The protests are losing momentum (Kyiv Independent, Aug 12). KIIS (Aug 5) finds 15% want elections now, up from 12%. Kuleba's Feb and Apr 2026 calls remain the best-documented qualifying statements.

No Gulf trade embargo on Iran was reported through Aug 13 (archive plus 3 searches). Kuwait shut its only Iranian school on Aug 6 after Iran repeatedly struck its power and desalination plants. Bahrain called Iran's attacks 'terrorist' at the UN (Aug 5) and jailed IRGC spies (Aug 11-12). Iran hit ADNOC tankers on Aug 8 and Aug 13, which the UAE called 'piracy', so Kuwait is moved level with Bahrain and the UAE is raised.

BBC (Aug 12) says Arsenal are reigniting their interest after an initial ~GBP30m approach fell short of Villa's GBP60m valuation, with Saliba now out for an 'extended period'. FootballTransfers (Aug 10) says Berta is in strong contact with Konsa's camp, while Villa try to agree a new contract and would rather sell Martinez (Football Insider, Aug 6). Konsa is still at Villa on post-World Cup rest (Aug 12-13). Arsenal are the only active bidder, so under conditional framing they are a clear favourite.

The archive (Jul 15-Aug 13) and a search found no new Nord Stream arrests since Serhii K. was indicted in Hamburg on Jul 2. The remaining suspects are believed to be in Ukraine, and Poland refused to surrender Zhuravlov in 2025. With 13 days of August gone and nothing reported, 'None' is nudged up.

Savinho has agreed personal terms with Spurs and submitted a transfer request (Romano, early Aug). Football Insider (Aug 8) says the deal is expected to be done before the window closes. Romano (Aug 13) still calls him a top Spurs target, with City asking GBP60-65m and wanting a replacement lined up. Milan's loan-with-obligation idea is unlikely to suit City. Under conditional framing Spurs are a strong favourite, with some hijack risk.

No sign through Aug 13 of Rocha Moya returning from leave or of a substitute governor being named. The Economist (Aug 4) calls him the 'then governor', and Sheinbaum disputes the US claims (Aug 5). With 8 days left, interim governor Bonilla is very likely still in charge on Aug 21.

AS (Aug 6) says his current plan is a US Open comeback, either directly or via Winston-Salem (from Aug 23), where he already has an invitation. His team says he will travel to New York either way (Aug 12), but no final decision was announced by Aug 12 and pundits call the US Open 50/50. Cincinnati is cut because he withdrew on Aug 4.

Baleba suffered ankle ligament damage in pre-season and will miss the start of the season (Sussex Express Aug 8; Sports Mole Aug 13). Romano (Aug 8) says Man Utd are 'not proceeding with the deal at the moment', and Reuters (Aug 13) lists United's summer spend as only Santos, Tielemans and Darlow. If a move still happens this window, United remain the most likely destination because Baleba has pushed hard to join them. Newcastle are flush with cash after selling Bruno and Tonali.

Maresca said on Aug 9 that Marmoush may want to leave for more minutes, and City want about EUR60-65m. Chronicle Live (Aug 9) says Newcastle are preparing a possible GBP55m bid and are best placed financially after big sales. Spurs (informal contacts, De Zerbi a fan) and Barcelona (an alternative to Alvarez) are also linked. Atletico, the leading suitor in July, do not appear in August reports.

Al-Ittihad announced his departure on Aug 6 after he turned down reduced terms, so he is a free agent. ESPN (via Terra, Aug 7) says he wants to return to European football and may consider MLS or Asia, and a move back to Brazil now looks remote. Ittihad are bidding for Fenerbahce's Amrabat to replace him (Goal, Aug 7), which could open a defensive-midfield slot at Fenerbahce.

The NYT (Aug 5) reports AIPAC is weighing 'tens of millions' for Rogers after El-Sayed won (UDP says no decision yet). Pro-Israel voices warn that backing a Republican in a swing state could backfire, and El-Sayed has dared AIPAC to 'burn your money' again (Aug 6-10). That makes a request from Rogers or his allies for AIPAC to stay out the most likely path, though no such report had appeared by Aug 12.

At Portland (Aug 8) Rosenqvist took pole by 0.018s from Palou, with Power 3rd and Hondas filling 10 of the top 12. It was Rosenqvist's second pole of 2026 after the Long Beach street race. Palou (6 poles this year) stays favourite on the new DC street circuit, while the Penske/Chevys qualified poorly (McLaughlin 14th, Malukas 9th).
Dimers (Aug 12) has a moneyline of Man Utd -240 and Hull +700 (about 67/21/12 with the margin removed), and its model gives 64/20.5/15.5. United beat Leeds in a friendly in Dublin on Aug 12.
